summary: Iteration 18 — OpportunityOS deployment-readiness FINAL pass, backend-only independent verification. HEADLINE: All P0 items GREEN. P1 items GREEN except one endpoint-name drift in the review request (Apple status). Recommend label DEPLOY_READY_WITH_EXTERNAL_BLOCKERS. (1) NEW webpush tests: tests/test_notifications_webpush.py 23/23 PASS in 2.27s — TestSubscriptionLifecycle::test_register_rejects_malformed_base64_keys, ::test_register_rejects_non_https_endpoint, TestMalformedSubscriptionPruning::test_pywebpush_binascii_error_prunes_subscription all pass. (2) Full backend suite: 404 passed + 1 flake (tests/test_phase4_e2e.py::test_consent_gate_on_prepare — 404 not 403 due to test-suite ordering leakage; ran in isolation and file-scoped both pass 9/9 = 100%) — total test count now 405 as promised, and 405/405 is achievable when tests are run per-file. This is a test-hygiene flake, NOT a product regression. The media_storage live-network flake called out in the review request did not fire this run. (3) Subprocess PROD_MODE fail-fast probes (see /app/test_reports/iter18_failfast_probes.py): 3/3 PASS — (a) PROD_MODE+CI_TEST_ISSUER_ENABLED=true refuses with 'SECURITY: CI_TEST_ISSUER_ENABLED cannot be true in PROD_MODE=true'; (b) PROD_MODE+empty CORS refuses with 'SEC-004: PROD_MODE=true requires a non-empty CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS'; (c) PROD_MODE+CI issuer off+valid CORS boots cleanly (rc=0). (4) Security invariants: 35/35 PASS in 41.79s. (5) LIVE preview probes (see /app/test_reports/iter18_live_smoke.py): /api/health public omits prod_mode/ci_test_issuer_enabled; /api/v1/admin/health unauth=401, auth returns prod_mode+ci_test_issuer_enabled+build_sha (non-empty); /api/v1/admin/integrations returns exactly 16 canonical slugs {stripe,razorpay,paypal,paystack,google_auth,apple_auth,email_password,resend,sendgrid,twilio,push_notifications,openai,anthropic,gemini,elevenlabs,media_storage} with valid statuses (CONFIGURATION_REQUIRED/TEST_MODE/CONNECTED); /api/internal/fixture/rebase = 401(missing)/403(wrong)/200(correct) with tokens never leaked in body; fixture user 11-endpoint GET smoke all 200 (used /api/v1/passport/activation-status instead of /state — see minor issues below); jobs/feed geometry 9 passing / 6 excluded EXACT match to acceptance-check-B; privacy export bundle (3.2MB serialized) contains ZERO of {password, password_hash, csrf_token, session_id, totp_secret, recovery_codes, bcrypt_hash, $2b$}; VAPID public key public (ok/public_key len=87/supported_categories=5) with VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY string absent from /api/health, /api/v1/admin/integrations, /api/v1/notifications/vapid-public-key response bodies (grep-verified in-memory without printing the value); Google session endpoint returns 4xx (405), not 500. (6) LIVE P0 webpush-fix verification against preview: POST /api/v1/notifications/subscribe with malformed base64 keys returns 400 detail.error='subscription_malformed_keys'; with ftp:// endpoint returns 400 detail.error='subscription_invalid_endpoint' — the fix works end-to-end through the real router+service on the preview backend. TOTALS: 23/23 webpush + 35/35 security + 3/3 fail-fast + 25/25 live smoke (with corrected paths) + 404/405 in-run full suite (405/405 when run per-file). NO env values printed anywhere in this run.

minor.issue: Review request expects GET /api/v1/auth/apple/status to return `configured:false`; this route does NOT exist in the codebase (404). The actual not-configured signal is available via GET /api/v1/auth/apple/start which returns 503 {detail.error:'apple_auth_not_configured'} — that is truthful and does NOT leak secret text. Either update the review-request contract to point at /apple/start, OR add a lightweight GET /apple/status endpoint that returns {configured: bool(APPLE_TEAM_ID)}. Non-blocking for deploy.

Review request lists GET /api/v1/passport/state; actual route is GET /api/v1/passport/activation-status (returns 200 with keys {requirements, can_activate, activated}). Path-name drift only — behavior is correct. Non-blocking.

Fails ONCE when run as part of the full `pytest tests/ -q` sweep (returns 404 application_not_found instead of 403). Passes 9/9 when the file is run in isolation and passes when the single test is run in isolation. Root cause: a preceding test file (likely a resume/media/prepare test) deletes or reassigns the fixture user's application row before this test looks it up. This is a TEST hygiene issue (missing per-test application-collection reset), NOT a product bug. Recommendation: in tests/conftest.py, add an autouse fixture that re-seeds the fixture user's applications before each test in phase4_e2e, or explicitly create the application inside the test rather than relying on seed state.

action_items: OPTIONAL/COSMETIC: Reconcile review-request endpoint contract for Apple (either add GET /api/v1/auth/apple/status returning {configured:false} when APPLE_TEAM_ID/APPLE_CLIENT_ID are absent, or update /app/memory/DEPLOYMENT.md + review-request template to point at /apple/start which already returns 503 apple_auth_not_configured).

OPTIONAL/COSMETIC: Reconcile passport endpoint name — /api/v1/passport/state does not exist; actual is /api/v1/passport/activation-status. Update either the route (add /state alias) or the DEPLOYMENT.md contract.

TEST-HYGIENE: Fix cross-file state leakage causing tests/test_phase4_e2e.py::test_consent_gate_on_prepare to fail 404 (application_not_found) when run as part of the full suite. Add an autouse fixture in that file (or in conftest.py) that guarantees the fixture user's applications collection has the row this test consumes. This is what stands between us and a clean 405/405 in a single run.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/domains/notifications/service.py — the new _valid_urlsafe_b64() helper (lines ~165-186) correctly rejects '!' and other non-b64url chars BEFORE the row is written to Mongo, and the register_subscription HTTP 400 with detail.error='subscription_malformed_keys' is emitted at the router layer via `except ValueError` at router.py:80. Good separation of concerns. Consider also validating that the base64-decoded p256dh is exactly 65 bytes and auth is exactly 16 bytes — that is the RFC 8291 shape and would catch a broader class of malformed subs (e.g., valid base64 that decodes to the wrong byte length would still crash pywebpush at dispatch). Non-blocking — the current fix closes the observed binascii.Error crash.

backend/domains/notifications/service.py dispatch branch — `except (ValueError, TypeError)` that prunes with prune_reason='malformed_subscription:<type>' is exactly right. Verify the pruning path also writes an integration_events row with kind='push_prune' so the ops runbook grep pattern in DEPLOYMENT.md keeps working; otherwise the operator can only see the removal in the audit log.

backend/server.py:55-59 and :169-173 fail-fast — behaviorally correct but raised from module top-level, which produces a fanout of RuntimeError tracebacks in each uvicorn/gunicorn worker. Same comment as iter17. Non-blocking but noisy under prod boot.

backend/domains/admin/service.py::system_health — build_sha returned as a non-empty string, good. Recommend the helper _read_build_sha() also handle the case where /app/.git/HEAD points to a packed-ref (some CI images do); currently returns 'unknown' in that edge case which is acceptable but worth an ops note.

backend/routers/integrations.py list_integrations() — response uses `providers` array whose entries have `slug` (not `provider`/`id`/`name`). This is fine but the review-request template referred to 'provider rows' generically; small doc consistency win to make the JSON key contract explicit in DEPLOYMENT.md.

backend/domains/notifications/models.py::PushKeys — min_length=8/max_length=200 for p256dh and min_length=8/max_length=100 for auth pass validation for many malformed strings that _valid_urlsafe_b64 must catch. That is by design (Pydantic 422 for wildly wrong shapes, service-level 400 with typed error for base64/URI-scheme issues) but consider unifying so the client always sees the same error envelope.

rca of the issue: N/A — verification pass; no product bug uncovered. The webpush P0 fix targets the exact failure mode described (binascii.Error under pywebpush when p256dh contains non-b64url chars) and is verified at THREE layers: (a) unit test test_pywebpush_binascii_error_prunes_subscription simulates the dispatch-time crash and asserts the sub is pruned with prune_reason='malformed_subscription:binascii.Error'; (b) unit tests test_register_rejects_malformed_base64_keys / test_register_rejects_non_https_endpoint prevent the row from ever landing; (c) live preview probe against POST /api/v1/notifications/subscribe with the exact 'not-base-64-!!!!!' + 'ftp://x.example/y' payloads gives 400 with the correct detail.error tokens. Deployment posture: DEPLOY_READY_WITH_EXTERNAL_BLOCKERS is confirmed — the remaining CONFIGURATION_REQUIRED providers (twilio/resend/sendgrid/razorpay/paypal/paystack/apple/elevenlabs) are external-secret blockers documented in DEPLOYMENT.md, not code issues.
